candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — staffing, assignment, safety, and professional responsibilities
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — fatigue, staffing, and patient safety
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize nurse fatigue as a shared organizational and individual patient-safety issue rather than solely a personal wellness concern.

options.A: Fatigue from long hours and inadequate staffing is a nurse and patient-safety risk that requires both organizational and individual mitigation strategies.
options.B: Fatigue should be treated only as a private wellness issue because it has no meaningful relationship to patient safety.
options.C: Extended overtime is the preferred long-term substitute for adequate staffing because fatigue does not materially affect error risk.
options.D: Nurses should avoid reporting fatigue because staffing and workload conditions are unrelated to professional safety responsibilities.

candidate.rationale: ANA identifies nurse fatigue as a workforce- and patient-safety issue and links long hours, heavy workload, inadequate staffing, and shiftwork with increased risk. ANA calls for shared mitigation through staffing/workload strategies and individual fatigue-management responsibilities. B through D contradict that position.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Nurse fatigue associated with long hours/workload/staffing conditions is a nurse and patient-safety risk requiring mitigation.
candidate.source_document_title: Addressing Nurse Fatigue to Promote Health, Safety, and Well-Being for All
candidate.source_locator: Statement of ANA Position and supporting discussion of long hours, workload, staffing, shiftwork, and safety mitigation
candidate.stem: A nurse is repeatedly scheduled for prolonged work hours because of chronic staffing shortages. Which patient-safety concern is most supported by current ANA guidance?
